messages:
lucas: hey team - quick tax/payroll puzzle. I was onboarded in 2025 through our Brazil EOR (LocalHire) until 2025-08-01, then converted to direct US employment effective 2025-08-15. I received Brazilian payslips (with INSS/FGTS) and LocalHire sent an earnings statement. Now I see a 2025 W-2 stub in my portal showing $0 for social security and Medicare, and no mention of the EOR months. Will the EOR income appear on my US W-2? worried about reporting and potential duplicate social security contributions.

maya (People Ops): thanks for flagging, @lucas. generally EOR/partner payroll runs separately and their payments do not show on the company's W-2. but there are edge cases if the EOR paid you as a US individual or if we processed a retrospective payment after conversion. tagging payroll + tax counsel to confirm. can you share the LocalHire docs or the EOR payslip IDs?

lucas: payslips: LH-2025-03, LH-2025-04, LH-2025-05. LocalHire withheld INSS and deposited FGTS per Brazilian rules. i also got a LocalHire year-end statement that lists total gross BRL 95,000. my portal shows a stub titled "W-2 preliminary" with wages = $12,000 (only post-conversion pay) and SS/Medicare = 0.

diego (Payroll): @lucas we see the LocalHire file in PAY-4201. quick guidance: payments made and taxed by the EOR in Brazil normally are not our payroll wages and should not appear on your US W-2. the zero SS/Medicare on the stub suggests those taxes weren't withheld by the company because the post-conversion pay may be below the payroll threshold or benefits setup pending. we will reconcile PAY-4201 and confirm if any retroactive gross-ups or reimbursements were posted.

ana (Tax Counsel): small correction: ana here. tax points: 1) EOR payments subject to Brazilian social taxes (INSS) are not automatically credited to US SS unless there is a totalization agreement. the US has a totalization agreement with Brazil? No, US-Brazil do not have a totalization agreement, so social contributions generally remain separate. 2) For US tax filing, you must report worldwide income if you are a US tax resident; EOR income may need to be reported on your US return, but foreign taxes can generally be credited (Form 1116) to avoid double taxation. 3) EOR income itself still usually won't be on the company's W-2 unless we paid you directly for those periods.

lucas: ok that helps. so should i expect any W-2c or 1099? and what about state withholding for the months when i was in Brazil but now resident in CA?

diego (Payroll): if we didn't process those earnings in our payroll, no W-2 or W-2c from us for that EOR income. If LocalHire issued any US forms (unlikely) they'd provide them. Regarding state: we only withhold state taxes for wages we paid. If you were not paid by us while physically in Brazil, there should be no CA withholding for those months. For post-conversion pay where SS/Medicare = 0, that's odd; might be a benefits enrollment or initial payroll setup issue. we'll run an audit and post any missing withholdings as supplemental deductions if needed. ETA: 3 business days.

ana (Tax Counsel): also recommend @lucas to keep LocalHire docs and be prepared to file for foreign tax credit when you do your 2025 return. we can provide a letter summarizing what company-paid wages we included on your W-2 if that helps your CPA.

maya (People Ops): action items: 1) lucas attach LocalHire payslips to PAY-4201; 2) payroll (diego) to audit and confirm whether any retro payments from the company were applied; 3) tax counsel (ana) to draft a verification letter for employee. payroll to update in 72 hours.

hr-bot: PAY-4201 updated  audit queued for diego  expected completion: 72 hours. :spiral_calendar:

lucas: attached the LH payslips to PAY-4201. thanks everyone 60a will hold docs for my accountant and watch for the audit results.
